newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ shares end lower after achieving 2-1/2 yr high.
newsitem.headline: NZ shares end lower after achieving 2-1/2 yr high.

text.p: 144 nil * NZSE-40 cap index -4.09 at 2,244.10 336 nil * NZSC cap index -4.85 at 4,430.15 285 nil * NZSE-10 cap index -0.92 at 1,134.41 370 -5 * Volume NZ$70 million. Futures untraded
New Zealand shares retreated from a new two-and-a-half year high reached in early trade to end a touch lower on Wednesday.

But brokers said the market showed resilience in the face of a weaker Dow and there had been good two-way business in the leaders, particularly Telecom, the Fletcher Challenge stocks and Carter Holt Harvey.
The NZSE-40 Capital Index closed 4.09 points lower at 2,244.10, having reached 2,252.20 during the session, its highest level since March 1994.
First NZ Capital broker Jim Patterson said that of the NZ$70 million turnover, trade in Telecom accounted for just under $20 million. The market leader ended the day a cent lower at $6.90.
INL gained 15 cents to $5.75, which brokers said was a response to excessive profit-taking after its price was driven up by the takeover bid for rival publisher Wilson and Horton.
Brokers said recent strength in the debt market, particularly in the long end, was helping equities, but the market was essentially being dominated by some large offshore buying orders.
However, investors were seen becoming more nervous as the October 12 general election neared.

"To be honest, I'm a little surprised that some of the offshore interest hasn't been a little bit more hesitant, given the uncertainty that now exists in terms of what will be a close result," said J.B. Were and Son broker Robert Gwyther.

Recent polls suggest the governing conservative National Party could be toppled by a centre-left grouping if the three main opposition parties are able to overcome their differences and form a coalition. -- Matthew Brockett (64 4) 473-3736
